designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: I drive an old car, so this one got a real laugh out of me. The clean icon grid looks smart, and PROBABLY FINE. lands right away. On the tee, though, the twenty icons and their tiny labels shrink to a speckled block, and you only get the joke up close. The airbag icon reads more like a lollipop than an airbag.
designs.fix: Print the grid bigger on the tee, or use fewer and larger lights (say 12), so the icons and PROBABLY FINE read from across a room.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Anyone with a dog smiles at the four 'Turn around.' steps, and '7. Sigh.' is the perfect ending. The loose brush dogs are warm and full of character, and it looks like a gift-shop print, not a gag shirt. The thin serif title and small italic captions get faint and tiny on the tee, so the punchline only works close up.
designs.fix: Enlarge the whole print on the tee and thicken the caption and title type, so 'Turn around.' x4 stays readable at a few meters.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Every cat owner has lived this, and the payoff panel with the smug, eyes-closed cat in the box next to the unused bed is lovely. The drawing is crisp and detailed. The joke is a familiar one, though, and the narrow vertical strip sits small and skinny on the tee, so it reads more like a sticker than a shirt.
designs.fix: Make the panels wider and the print larger so it fills the chest, and give the cat in panel 2 a clearer snub (turned away or walking off), so the middle beat reads instantly.
